title: Choosing funds that complement each other
objectives: Name four ways a new fund can complement existing funds.
Check overlap before adding any new fund.
body_md:
Choosing funds that complement each other: different market-cap focus (large vs mid vs small). Different style (growth vs value) or approach (active vs index). Different geography (an international fund, where suitable). Low overlap on a tool, checked before adding any new fund.

> **Investor takeaway:** Before adding, let's see what it does that your current funds don't.
example: Adding a value fund to a growth-heavy portfolio, or an international fund for geography — each adds something different, checked on a tool first.
say: Check overlap before adding any new fund.
Different style or geography can complement; same stocks cannot.
never: Add last year's top fund without checking.

check.q: A client wants to add last year's top flexi-cap fund. What do you do first?
o: Check its overlap with existing funds; ask what job it would do; add only if it brings something different
Replace all existing funds with it
Ignore overlap and follow the rating
check.why: Check its overlap with existing funds; ask what job it would do; add only if it brings something different.

check.q: Which new fund complements a growth-heavy portfolio?
o: Another growth fund holding the same stocks
A value fund with low overlap, checked on a tool first
check.why: Different style (growth vs value) or approach (active vs index). Low overlap on a tool, checked before adding any new fund.

check.q: Before adding any new fund, always:
o: Check its overlap with what the client already holds
check.why: Low overlap on a tool, checked before adding any new fund.
